lines: An oscillator whose waveform is drawn by one to six control points, with a built-in amplifier and an end-of-cycle trigger
Curves the waveform to the right of that point: straight at 0, and a quadratic Bezier curve bending either way from there
Modulates the curve of the waveform to the right of that point, over -5 to +5V
Sets the value of that point, -1 to 1, which is one corner of the drawn waveform
Modulates the value of that point, over -5 to +5V
Sets how many of the six points make up the waveform, one to six
Sets how many points make up the waveform, at a volt per point
Sets the pitch of the oscillator, C4 by default; in LFO mode the frequency is divided by 100
Tunes the pitch in fine steps around the frequency knob
Scales the output from -100% to +100%, inverting the waveform below 0, and takes an envelope for a built-in VCA
Modulates the output level, and takes an envelope to duck the output while the waveform changes
Raises the pitch by one octave per volt
Limits the output to -5 to +5V, which the curved waveform can otherwise exceed
A 10V trigger at the end of every waveform cycle, for syncing a scope or another module to the waveform
The generated waveform, -5 to +5V at full amplitude
Note — with only point A active the output is a static voltage set by that point and the amplitude, and pitch, fine tune and the curves do nothing
Menu — Frequency: chooses VCO, or LFO where the frequency is divided by 100
Menu — CV Param Mode sets how every CV input acts on its knob or slider: Offset adds the CV to it, Follow sets it from the CV, Attenuate scales the CV by it
Menu — CV Input Slew smooths every CV input, which stops abrupt CV changes clicking: None, 1ms, 5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms or 100ms
Menu — Clamp CV Values keeps a value driven by CV inside the range of its knob or slider; switched off, the value can go past that range
Menu — Antialiasing switches the oversampling that reduces aliasing at high frequencies
Menu — Auto-Duck dips the output while the waveform is being changed

The oversampling factor and filter frequency behind Antialiasing are not stated in any source, so no numbers are quoted.
